domain: Health - maternal care services / vital statistics (cesarean delivery monitoring)
prediction_question: At the publication instant of complete-year T SINASC live-birth data for Brazil (America/Sao_Paulo; the publisher's own TABNET base is stamped final for year T no later than early December T+1 - measured: 'Dados finais disponíveis até 2024 - data de extração 02/12/2025'), will a municipality's cesarean share among resident live births fall by at least 2 percentage points from year T to complete calendar year T+2 - the next complete year whose every month lies after that instant? A useful prediction identifies which municipalities will move against the still-rising national cesarean level (60.6% of resident births in 2024), informing where maternal-care policy attention (SUS maternity audits, cesarean-reduction programs) is likely to matter two seasons ahead.
prediction_time: One sentence: the prediction is made at the final-publication instant of complete-year T SINASC data (no later than early December T+1, America/Sao_Paulo), using only complete calendar years <= T as features, about the cesarean share of complete year T+2. Dated example (America/Sao_Paulo, UTC-03:00, no DST): T = 2024; feature event window = births with DTNASC in 1996-2024 (each year final per the publisher's FINAL/PRELIMINAR/PRÉVIA ladder; earliest feature events 1996-01-01); first-available timestamps and version = the 2024 CSV resource was created 2024-06-11 (preview) and the publisher's TABNET base is stamped final for 2024 at extraction 2025-12-02, the whole CSV archive being last refreshed 2026-05-08 (current-vintage; no historical vintages exist); eligibility cutoff (at the instant, from instant-visible data only): municipality had >= floor F resident live births in year T (F in {100,200,500} measured); prediction instant = 2025-12-02 (the publisher-stamped date on which complete-year 2024 data is final); target window = complete year T+2 = 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31, every month after the instant. No part of the target window precedes the instant; the 2025 preliminares (CKAN resource created 2025-10-21) and any 2026 previews are excluded from features by design.
target_definition: Binary label for municipality m and publication instant of year T: 1 if cesarean_share(m, T+2) <= cesarean_share(m, T) - 0.02, else 0, where cesarean_share(m, Y) = count(PARTO == 2 among resident live births of m in Y) / count(all resident live births of m in Y) (denominator includes the small Ignorado stream; nationally <1% since 1996 - measured). Source columns: PARTO (dictionary: 'Tipo de parto: 1- Vaginal; 2- Cesário; 9- Ignorado'), CODMUNRES (IBGE residence municipality), DTNASC (birth date) - the label source columns are excludable from shipped features by construction (ship lagged municipality-year aggregates only). Margin 2pp is provisional and measured at three floors; the rise-direction label (>= +2pp) and a national-median-exceedance alternative are measured as calibration options; final margin fixed per split window at construction, before any scoring.

split_strategy: PROPOSED, measured on sampled transitions (all counts computed from the publisher's own TABNET aggregates, 2026-11-02; full-panel exact counts are the first construction step on the worker - sampled counts are never presented as full counts). Unit = (municipality, transition T -> T+2), one row per municipality per target year T+2, target years spaced annually. Windows disjoint by target year: train targets 2000-2012, eval targets 2013-2018, holdout targets 2019-2024 (27 potential target years 1998-2024 with T >= 1996 feature history). Measured sampled transitions inside the windows (floor = min resident births in T and T+2): train: 1998->2000 n=3334/2231/962 (floors 100/200/500) decline>=2pp 34.9/33.8/30.1%, rise>=2pp 37.6/37.2/34.9%; 2002->2004 n=3556/2360/1008 decline 15.4/13.5/10.6%, rise 59.9/59.9/60.3%; 2009->2011 n=3349/2205/944 decline 12.9/10.7/8.2%, rise 67.5/68.3/67.7%; eval: 2012->2014 n=3349/2177/932 decline 22.6/19.9/19.2%, rise 50.9/50.7/45.6%; 2014->2016 n=3308/2162/927 decline 41.1/40.8/42.7%, rise 30.1/28.0/21.0%; holdout: 2017->2019 n=3298/2178/935 decline 25.2/23.1/21.0%, rise 44.7/42.6/39.4%; 2019->2021 n=3260/2148/907 decline 25.1/23.4/20.6%, rise 45.1/43.9/41.0%; 2022->2024 n=3132/1966/833 decline 18.6/15.7/12.4%, rise 56.4/58.2/55.7%. Both classes present in every measured (transition x floor) cell (24/24, computed). Cluster structure: rows within a target year share the national era (the rise-dominant 1998-2014 era vs the plateau/decline era after 2015 - measured: national share 32.0% 1994, 50.0% 2009, 60.59% 2024); the municipality is a repeating unit; independence scale = the target year (27 instants). Municipality mesh drift measured: 5560 distinct codes 2002-2008, 5565 2009-2013, 5570 2014-2024 (new municipalities; handled by eligibility + code-presence, recorded as a construction caveat).

review: Five contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (all measured 2026-11-02, commands in notes.md, outputs in probe/out/). (1) Redistribution: SUPPORTED - dataset-specific CKAN licence cc-by (quote in license_evidence), with the site-footer BY-ND 3.0 conflict recorded and a named escalation path; residual risk noted, not hidden. (2) Prediction timing: SUPPORTED for the stated contract - instant = publisher-stamped final publication of complete year T (measured bound: no later than early December T+1), features = final complete years <= T (preliminares/previews excluded by design), target = complete year T+2 whose every month follows the instant (dated example in prediction_time; a 2025-12-02 instant cannot call any month of 2026 past); every feature column documented by the publisher's dictionary; vintage limitation recorded: historical vintages do not exist (archive refreshed 2026-05-08), so the panel is a clearly-labelled current-vintage retrospective with no operational point-in-time claim for history - the as-of policy and its coverage are stated, not assumed. (3) Target: SUPPORTED - label from PARTO==2 counts over CODMUNRES x DTNASC-year; label columns excludable (ship lagged aggregates only); missing-parto (Ignorado) stream measured (< 1.5% since 1996, < 0.2% since 2002) and kept in the denominator, so 'no recorded event' is not confused with observed absence. (4) Split capacity: SUPPORTED on evidence - 8 sampled transitions spanning 1998-2024, both classes in all 24 (transition x floor) cells, 833-3556 eligible municipalities per transition; UNMEASURED: exact per-window counts for all 27 target years (needs the ~3 GB CSV pass on a worker - recorded as the first construction step with acceptance criteria, never a blocker discovered after construction). (5) Contribution: SUPPORTED - novelty check recorded, verdict differentiated (mechanical search over HF/Zenodo/arXiv/web: microdata mirrors exist, national/FU-level ARIMA trend projections and individual-level clinical cesarean prediction exist; no municipality-year share-transition benchmark with temporal splits). Cross-row self-answer risk (a municipality's T+2 share is a later row's feature) is identified: construction must enforce the restricted prediction protocol per docs/PREDICTION-CONTRACT.md (pre-aggregated feature matrices, no unit x year join keys in solver-visible files). Cluster dependence: target-year era drift is measured (rise-share falls from ~60-68% pre-2014 to ~21-56% after), so scoring must cluster by target year. Known-event fixture: national 2024 share 60.59% must reproduce from the CSV channel.

prior_art: Temporal trends and projections of caesarean sections in Brazil (Cad Saude Publica / Cien Saude Coletiva 2023, ARIMA 1994-2019 series); HF dataset SidneyBissoli/sinasc (microdata mirror, not a task); healthbR R package; preterm-birth risk stratification Brazil (populational ML, individual level, 2023); neonatal mortality targeting study (SINASC+SIM+CNES linkage 2015-2017)
novelty_check.theirs: DATASUS/SUS publishes the raw SINASC microdata itself (and third parties mirror it: HF SidneyBissoli/sinasc Parquet mirror 1994-2022, healthbR download helper); the literature offers aggregate ARIMA/joinpoint trend projections of cesarean rates at national/macro-region/FU level (SciELO CSC 2023) and individual-level clinical prediction of cesarean delivery from maternal characteristics (US NCHS models, Ethiopia ML study) plus individual-level SINASC-based ML for preterm birth and neonatal mortality - none formulate a municipality-year share-change prediction task with temporal splits and scored baselines
novelty_check.ours: A national municipality-year cesarean-share transition panel built from the official SINASC open microdata channel: at the publication instant of complete-year T data (measured calendar), predict whether a municipality's cesarean share among resident live births declines by a fixed margin in complete year T+2 (entirely future at the instant), with eligibility floor, temporal splits over 1998-2025 and conditional-rate baselines - a benchmark, not a data dump
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
